subject: Pricing annex harmonization & SKU migration — redline questions
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoody.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoody.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoody.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing annex — a few redline clarifications and SKU migration impact

Hi Karthik / team,

Thanks for sending the updated Order Form and Pricing Annex. We did an initial pass with procurement + legal and have three areas that need clarification before we can sign:

1) SKU conversion / migration language — how does the floor/minimum interact when we migrate existing SKUs into a new bundle? Is the floor applied per-SKU or at the aggregate account level?
2) Embedding/feature caps — there appears to be a separate cap for embeddings; please confirm whether token caps are additive or inclusive of generation tokens.
3) Stabilizer true‑up timing — the draft calls for an annual true‑up; we prefer quarterly true‑ups during year one of migration.

We've attached ACME_OrderForm_20280115_redline.docx with inline suggestions from our side. Can we schedule 30 minutes this week to walk through? Available windows: Wed 1/17 10–12 PT or Thu 1/18 14–16 PT.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Senior Sourcing Manager — Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_20280115_redline.docx (docx, 112 KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing annex — a few redline clarifications and SKU migration impact

Samantha — thanks for the detailed pass and the redline. We appreciate the specific asks; quick responses below and we'll follow with consolidated language.

- SKU conversion / migration: intent is aggregate-account floor for commercial accounting simplicity, but we also want to avoid double-charging during a migration window. Proposal: treat converted SKUs as "migration credit" for the first 90 days after cutover, after which they count toward the aggregate floor.
- Embeddings cap: embeddings are measured in embedding units and are separate from generation token usage; for billing we treat them as additive units (i.e., they do not draw from generation token caps). We'll show an example mapping in the annex.
- True‑up timing: we can agree to quarterly true‑ups for Year 1 migration period; revert to annual thereafter.

Routing plan: looping in Legal (Laura) to confirm the exact redline text we can accept without opening broader exposure. Marissa / Jonas — can you confirm whether finance is comfortable with the 90‑day migration credit and the one‑time reconciliation credit Karthik mentioned on the call?

Propose we take a 30 min sync on Wed 1/17 at 10:30 PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a consolidated redline PDF (RDW-PricingAnnex-v2.pdf).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW-PricingAnnex-v2.pdf (pdf, 84 KB)

From: Derek Li <derek.li@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing annex — a few redline clarifications and SKU migration impact

Karthik / Marissa —

Acme legal reviewed RDW-PricingAnnex-v2.pdf and the attached Order Form redline. Main legal concern: the current "floor" language could be read to permit Redwood to apply the floor on a per‑SKU basis at your discretion. To avoid disputes we need explicit language that the floor is calculated on an aggregate, account‑level basis and that any credits for SKU conversions are documented and non‑retroactive beyond the migration window.

Suggested change (inline in their docx, but restating here): replace "floor" sentence in Exhibit B with: "The Minimum Annual Commitment (the 'Floor') shall be calculated on an aggregate basis across all SKUs and services enumerated in this Order Form. During a Migration Window (defined below), converted SKUs shall receive a Migration Credit and shall not be counted toward the Floor for the duration of the Migration Window."

Also seeking clarity on dispute resolution timing for true‑ups (we prefer 60 days after quarter close).

Happy to review your consolidated redline.

—Derek
Derek Li, Counsel — Acme Health
Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_20280115_redline.docx (docx, 112 KB)

Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 10:24:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Pricing annex — legal suggested compromise language

Team,

I reviewed Acme's inline and Derek's note. We can accept the aggregate-floor framing but want to preserve Redwood's ability to operationalize billing on a SKU-level for reporting. Proposed compromise text (clean):

"Minimum Annual Commitment (the 'Floor') shall be calculated on an aggregate basis across all SKUs and Redwood-managed services. For the purposes of billing and reporting, Redwood may present Floor calculations broken down by SKU, but such breakdowns are for informational purposes only and do not modify the aggregate Floor calculation. During a documented Migration Window (not to exceed 180 days unless mutually agreed), any SKU conversions will receive a Migration Credit. Migration Credits are one-time adjustments applied in the first reconciliation following conversion and shall not be counted as refunds or rebates beyond the reconciliation period.

We should offer: a 90‑day standard Migration Window; ability to extend to 180 days by written agreement; quarterly true‑ups in Year 1; 60‑day dispute window post‑quarter (as Acme asks).

Commercial concession to close: offer a one‑time migration credit equal to 3% of estimated first‑year ARR applied at first reconciliation. Finance (Jonas) — please confirm that 3% is acceptable. If yes, I'll insert the clean redline and we can send to Acme with a tracked doc.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: (suggested redline text included inline)

Date: Sun, 22 Jan 2028 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing annex — consolidated reply and proposed concession

Samantha / Derek — thanks for your patience. Per Laura's guidance and internal alignment, please find our consolidated position below and attached (RDW-Consolidated-Commercial-Reply.docx).

Summary of changes we can accept:
- Aggregate Floor calculation confirmed. We'll add explicit language that SKU-level breakdowns are informational only and do not alter the aggregate Floor.
- Migration Window: standard 90 days; extension to 180 days by mutual written agreement. Migration Credits applied in first reconciliation after conversion.
- True‑up cadence: quarterly true‑ups for Year 1, annual thereafter. Disputes to be raised within 60 days of reconciliation.
- Commercial concession: Redwood will apply a one‑time Migration Credit equal to 3% of the estimated first‑year ARR (applied at first reconciliation).

We're proposing a short call to finalize and sign — Tue 1/24 at 10:30 PT (30 min). If that works for you we'll send a calendar invite with the tracked doc.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
